  MEETING OF THE

  MONDAY, OCTOBER 4, 2021 AT 7:00 P.M.
  VIA TELECONFERENCE

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Community interest provides the Public
Safety Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 1st Monday of every month.

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires
a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact
the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300-0705 prior
to the meeting for assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)
Members of the Public Safety Commission may teleconference into the meeting without noticing
each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
As a precaution to protect staff, our constituents, and appointed officials, the City is following
the State and County Health Department’s current Health Officer recommendations to prevent
and reduce transmission of COVID0-19 by holding meetings via teleconference

Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
otherwise electronically:

  1) Public comment will be accepted by email to fire@cityofsanmarino.org before or during
  the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to be read by the
  Committee during public comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the
  interest of time.

FROM:  Police Chief John N Incontro
BY:  Vanessa Guillen, Administrative Assistant

DATE:  October 4, 2021

SUBJECT:  POLICE DEPARTMENT UPDATE REPORT AUGUST 2021

BACKGROUND

Each month the Police Department provides a brief update on crime, traffic issues, and other
items of interest to the public and to the Public Safety Committee.

DISCUSSION

This report will provide the Public Safety Commission with information for the month of
August 2021. The Pandemic has resulted in altering police service in our community. We have
had to modify the department’s community engagement, neighborhood watch programs, and
limited our contact with others to lessen the potential of infection spread. The services at the
front desk have been curtailed, limiting one on one contact, other than emergencies or
reporting of serious crimes.

As of August 31, 2021, Part 1 crimes have overall decreased by 31.66% when compared to
August 2020. The city suffered thirteen larcenies in August, related to property left outside,
thefts from unlocked vehicles, and thefts by fraud. The city suffered one residential burglary,
where the residence was vacant and under construction.

INVESTIGATIVE FOLLOW-UP

As of August 31, 2021 the Detective Bureau completed the following activates;
  • The Detective Bureau filed 12 cases for prosecution with the Alhambra District
  Attorney’s Office.
  • One search warrant was obtained for ongoing investigations.

  Page 5 of 25
 COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT

With continued COVID-19 concerns, the department has had to limit their community
engagement. During the month of August, the Police Department hosted a virtual
Neighborhood Watch meeting via Zoom. The motor officers participated in a Bicycle Rodeo at
Valentine Elementary School, and this year the Police Department was able to host National
Night Out at Lacy Park.

PERSONNEL UPDATE

The department currently has 28 of the 30 sworn positions filled. We currently have one cadet
in the final phase of the background process and another cadet in the background phase of the
process. The department has two sworn position vacancies and two cadet position vacancies.

TECHNOLOGY

The Flock Safety Cameras installed throughout the City have assisted in alerting officers to
stolen vehicles through the city, for the month of August the Flock Safety Cameras assisted in
one arrest.

TRAFFIC REPORT

A radar traffic trailer was placed at three separate intersections during the month of August.
From August 1 to August 15, the trailer was placed at the intersections of Sierra Madre
Boulevard and Robles Avenue, from August 16 to August 22, it was placed at 2701 Huntington
Drive, and from August 23 to August 31, it was placed at the intersections of Lorain Road and
Ridgeway Road.

Traffic enforcement is based upon three areas; traffic complaints from the community,
observation of violations by officers, and traffic collision data. The Department maintains a list
of traffic complaint locations and traffic collision data for traffic enforcement. As part of our
traffic collision investigations, we will look for other issues that may have been a contributory
factor in the collision. Those factors could be distracted driving, engineering, or environmental.
The traffic data utilized for traffic enforcement are the top five locations for traffic collisions and
the top Primary Collision Factors (PCF’s), or causes of the traffic collisions.

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

DATE:  October 4, 2021

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT REPORT

MONTHLY PERFORMANCE METRICS
Since the last Public Safety Commission Meeting, the Fire Department has submitted the August
Monthly Performance Metrics to the City Council. A copy of the report has been included in
this update. The report includes the number of responses made by the Department, training
hours, Fire Prevention inspections, and the Department’s cardiac arrest performance for the
month of August.

COVID-19 RESPONSE
San Marino Fire Department personnel continue to follow department personal protective
equipment protocols during emergencies for the safety of firefighters and patients. Additionally,
paramedics follow all current Los Angeles County Department of Health Services protocols for
the evaluation and transportation of patients requiring emergency medical services.

As of September 23, 2021, 84.7% of San Marino residents age 12 and older have received at least
one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. Additionally, 97.1% of youth age 12-17 and 97.3% of San
Marino residents age 65 and older have received at least one dose.
Residents who received their COVID-19 vaccination within the State of California may request
a digital copy of their COVID-19 vaccine record by visiting https://myvaccinerecord.cdph.ca.gov/.

MOBILE VACCINATION PROGRAM
The San Marino Fire Department is currently in discussion with the Los Angeles County
Department of Public Health to revive the “Mobile Vaccination for Homebound 65+ Population”
program. The revived program would provide previous recipients of the mobile vaccination
program with booster shots once available.

FIREFIGHTER OF THE YEAR
Fire Captain Dominic Petta was named Firefighter of the Year and recently honored by the
Rotary Club of San Marino as well as San Marino Masonic Lodge 408. Captain Petta was named
Firefighter of the Year based upon his demonstrated leadership, care, compassion, technical

  Page 11 of 25
 proficiency, and dedication to the residents of the City. This year, Fire Captain Dominic Petta
led several significant capital projects that resulted in a safer, more comfortable living quarters
for all fire department members for years to come. This effort involved several months of
budgeting, planning, and effort to complete these projects with the labor provided by Captain
Petta and fire department personnel. Captain Petta regularly distinguishes himself by his calm,
caring and compassionate demeanor, and he is well known to residents. Captain Petta is also
regularly the recipient of thanks and praise for these qualities and is deserving of the 2021
Firefighter of the Year.

TRAINING
Fire Department personnel participated in an estimated 502 hours of training during the month
of September. Final training hours will be included in the September Performance Metrics Report.
The Department currently has 4 probationary firefighters, and training efforts continue to focus
almost exclusively on Probationary Firefighter training.
Training during the month of September included continuing EMS education with the UCLA
Nurse Educator, building construction, and training at the Alhambra Training Tower.
In September, San Marino Fire Department Command Staff along with Chief Officers of Area “C”
and the Verdugo Fire Communications Center, participated in Active Shooter Training. This
training was offered as part of a quarterly training plan to provide opportunities for Chief Officers
to receive ongoing training that ensures a consistent, systematic development of command
organization, consistent strategy and tactics, and ensures a safe and effective deployment of
resources across multiple agencies. The annual training plan was spearheaded by San Marino Fire
Chief Mario Rueda and approved by the Area “C” Fire Chief’s Training subcommittee.

WILDFIRE PREPAREDNESS
As the fire season begins in Southern California, moderate to severe drought continues to persist
across our region. So far, our region has seen well below normal fire activity. However,
beginning this month, live fuel moistures in Los Angeles County have just reached critical levels.
The fire department is wrapping up brush inspections in our Very High Fire Severity Zone to
ensure that in the event of a fire in our City, the Firefighters have every opportunity to save life
and property. Further information on our vegetation management program can be obtained at
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org/brushclearance.

EARTHQUAKE RETROFITTING GRANTS
The application period for the CEA Earthquake Brace & Bolt Program grants for seismic retrofit
of older homes will open during the 4th week of October. Earthquake Brace + Bolt (EBB) helps
homeowners lessen the potential for damage during an earthquake. EBB offers a grant of up to
$3,000  toward  a  seismic  retrofit  for  qualifying  older  houses.  Visit
https://www.earthquakebracebolt.com to sign up to be notified when registration opens.

SIGNIFICANT INCIDENTS
On September 19, Engine 91, RA 91, and Battalion 9 were dispatched with Pasadena Truck 32 to
a vehicle into structure and broken gas main on the 1200 block of San Marino Avenue. Engine 91

 arrived on scene and discovered a vehicle had struck a 2-story residence with leaking natural gas from
a sheared gas meter. Fire Department personnel quickly controlled the gas and deemed the property
safe for the home owner to occupy. No occupants within the home were injured. The Fire
Department treated the occupants of the vehicle and transported one patient to a local area hospital.

Strike Team Deployments

Captain Nick Maza returned from his deployment to the Dixie Fire on Sunday, September 5 after 23
days. As of September 30, the Dixie Fire is 94% contained; 100% containment is estimated to occur
on October 30, 2021.

Engine 91 returned from its deployment to the Caldor Fire on Sunday, September 12 after 12 days.
As of September 30, the Caldor Fire is 83% contained; 100% containment is estimated to occur on
October 16, 2021. On Sunday, September 5, the San Marino Fire Department received the following
message from a former Southern California resident on the City’s Facebook page:

A very big and hearty shout out to the San Marino fire truck crew, seen a few short minutes ago here
in Carson City, Nevada. Seeing the truck turn from William street/hwy50, onto carson st.

FY 2021-22 DEPARTMENT OBJECTIVES
  •  Continue to lead the City’s response to COVID-19.
  •  Continue to provide accurate measurements of Fire Department performance.
  •  Place into service new Rescue Ambulance 91.
  •  Conduct a review of the current Community Emergency Response Training (CERT) and
  develop a “Citizen Fire Academy” for residents’ participation.
  •  Develop a City-wide Evacuation Plan for review and approval by the Disaster Council
  and City Council.
  •  Improve the City’s Emergency Preparedness through the completion of the upgrade to
  the Emergency Operations Center, including new phone and computer set up, new
  mapping, and staff training.
  •  Review and revise the City’s Emergency Operations Plan for City Council adoption.
  •  Conduct a City-wide emergency operations exercise with City staff, Department Heads,
  and the School District.
  •  Complete necessary upgrades to the Emergency Operations Center in coordination
  with the Parks and Public Works Department.

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY PERFORMANCE REPORT

The attached San Marino Fire Department August 2021 Performance Report represents the
incident data reports intended to meet the Improvement Goals referenced in the March 2, 2018
Report to City Council titled; Implementation Plan Fire Department Deployment Study. The
Fire Department has been working closely with Verdugo Fire Dispatch (VFD) to ensure the
accuracy of the data being reported. Some of the data sets are not currently available from VFD
and are listed as N/A. VFD has been made aware of the San Marino Fire Department’s interest
in pursuing the data associated with the fire and life safety goals as approved by the City Council.
Improvement Goal A in the Report recommended the following:

Call Processing Goals
9-1-1 calls will be answered at the primary PSAP (Public Safety Answering Point) San Marino
Police Department within 15 seconds, 95% of the time.

9-1-1 calls will be transferred from the primary PSAP to Verdugo Fire Dispatch within 30 seconds
from the time answered, 95% of the time.
This data is not available.

Recommended Turnout Goal
Response personnel shall initiate the response of a unit capable of mitigating an incident to a
priority fire and rescue incident 80 seconds from notification 90% of the time.

Response personnel shall initiate response to all other priority incidents within 60 seconds from
notification 90% of the time.

Recommended First-Due Response Time Goal
The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at a priority
fire or rescue incident within 5 minutes and 20 seconds from notification of response personnel,
90 percent of the time.

  Page 14 of 25
 The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at all other
priority incidents within 5 minutes from notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.

Recommended Response Force Goal
The full effective response force shall arrive at a moderate risk structure fire within 9 minutes
and 20 seconds of notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.
This data is not available.

Cardiac Arrest Data
The Cardiac Arrest data set includes the total number of cardiac arrest patients treated by
Firefighter/Paramedics. We always pray that the number is as low as possible. The more
important data sets are the subsequent measures which include the number of times the
Firefighter/Paramedics are successful in returning a patient’s spontaneous circulation (ROSC) –
our goal with ROSC is always 100%. Saving lives is why the Fire Department exists; unfortunately,
this is not always in our control. Lastly, the subsequent data sets measure the percentages of
correct treatments performed by the Firefighter/Paramedics.

City of San Marino COVID-19 Response
San Marino Fire Department personnel continue to follow department personal protective
equipment protocols during emergencies for the safety of firefighters and patients. Additionally,
paramedics follow all current Los Angeles County Department of Health Services protocols for
the evaluation and transportation of patients requiring emergency medical services.

COVID incidents increased during the month of August. The San Marino Fire Department’s
partner agencies in the San Gabriel Valley responded to 275 COVID related incidents in the
month of August, the most responses in one month since January 2021. There have been no
COVID incidents requiring emergency medical services within the City of San Marino since March
2021.

As of September 16, 2021, 84.2% of San Marino residents age 12 and older have received at least
one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. Additionally, 96.5% of youth age 12-17 and 96.7% of San
Marino residents age 65 and older have received at least one dose.

Residents who received their COVID-19 vaccination within the State of California may request
a digital copy of their COVID-19 vaccine record by visiting https://myvaccinerecord.cdph.ca.gov/.

Overtime
As of July 18, 2021 the Fire Department has achieved full staffing. During the month of August,
the Fire Department dispatched one Firefighter Field Observer to the Dixie Fire and one engine

by the State of California.

 TO:  Chair Boozell and members of the Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Michael Throne, PE, Director of Parks & Public Works/City Engineer

DATE:  October 47, 2021

SUBJECT:  SEPTEMBER THROUGH OCTOBER PARKS AND PUBLIC WORKS
  UPDATE

BACKGROUND

Please accept the following as a summary of notable activities that have been accomplished, are
underway or are planned for the balance of this month through your next regularly scheduled
commission meeting.

DISCUSSION

Follow-up Items from Prior Commission Meetings
•  No items.

Projects in or near Construction
•  The FY 20-21 street rehabilitation project is wrapping-up with the contractor focusing on
  final striping and punchlist items. They completed on schedule (September 15). The project
  is anticipated to be accepted as complete in November.
•  The street light poles have been replaced on Bellwood Drive. However, due to supply chain
  problems, the contractor cannot get the acorn-style lamp globe adapter ring to affix it onto
  the pole. It is hoped that this will be resolved in the coming weeks. [No update to report]

Projects in Design/Out-to-Bid

•  The Department will be recommending a consultant to design this fiscal year’s street
  rehabilitation program project to the City Council on October 13.
•  City staff and the architect continued to work with the San Marino Center (SMC) community
  task force on detailed design work to renovate SMC into a new community facility. Work
  also continued on the preparation of a focused environmental impact report. The plans are
  at the 95% stage and have been submitted for plan check.
•  Dudek engineers continue to work on the plans to upgrade of our 3 sanitary sewer lift stations
  as part of the lift station improvement program. They are at the 70% design plans stage.
  Advertisement for construction bids is planned for early October. [No update to report]

  Page 19 of 25
 Projects under Study/Analysis

•  The pavement restriping changes recommended to improve pedestrian safety along Granada
  Avenue and at the northwest corner of Huntington Drive and Sierra Madre Boulevard were
  presented to the City Council on September 8 for their approval. However, due to the length
  of that Council meeting, this item was continued to their October 13 meeting.
  Commissioners are free to attend the meeting to share their thoughts on this work.
•  The Department has continued to receive requests for the “Caution
  Watch For…” signs and is placing them in select neighborhoods with
  a positive response from the residents. At the recommendation of
  the City’s traffic engineer, the Department is going to substitute W11-
  15 signs (see nearby) because the sign meets the same need and is an
  official traffic control device approved by state and federal
  governments. Use of an approved sign will help protect the City from
  liability and allow better enforcement of the vehicle code by the Police Department. [No
  update to report]

Maintenance Activities

•  The Parks and Public Works Department is pursuing its normal fall maintenance schedule
  activities

Other Department Activities

•  The Department continues to support the City’s Covid-19 response plan
•  Interview for the PW manager are scheduled for this week.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission receive and file this report. If the Commission concurs
with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

“I move to receive and file the October 2021 Parks and Public Works Department update.”
